claims.source_quote_ar: ثم ثنى اللَّه سبحانه في شأنهم بتمثيل آخر ليكون كشفا لحالهم بعد كشف، وإيضاحا غب إيضاح.
claims.claim_ar: ثنى/تمثيل (مقابلة) في ترتيب الصور البيانية: مواجهة حالة تزيين الدنيا للكافرين ببيان حال المؤمنين في الآخرة (فوقهم يوم القيامة) لإظهار التضاد والتقابل بين الحالتين.
claims.claim_en: Use ofثنى/representation (an instance of muqabalah/contrast): the pairing contrasts the disbelievers' adornment of worldly life with the believers' elevation on the Day of Resurrection to highlight opposition between the two states.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited source (Zamakhshari) discusses ثنى/تمثيل with examples; mapping that general discussion to this specific ayah is interpretive and would benefit from cross-checking with additional rhetorical/tafsir sources requested by the user (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, etc.).
claims.rhetorical_effect: Heightens moral contrast and warns the audience by juxtaposing temporary worldly allure with lasting eschatological status; increases emphasis on eventual divine justice.

claims.claim_ar: وقف/وصل في الموصول (الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ): إمكان قراءته أو تأويله على وجهين (موصول/مقتطع) يؤثر على الوقف والحرْكَة البلاغية ويزيد أو ينقص من حدة التوكيد على صفة المؤمنين مقابل الكافرين.
claims.claim_en: Pause/join (fasl_wasl) in the relative clause 'الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ': the clause can be read as connected or as a detached (mutaqta') description, and that syntactic choice affects rhetorical emphasis of the believers' trait in contrast to the disbelievers.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source (Zamakhshari) treats the alternative readings and rhetorical effect of موصول vs مقتطع; applying this specifically to the relative in the ayah is plausible but hinges on reader/recitation practice — recommend checking other tafsir/بلاغة specialists (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki) for stronger confirmation.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Controls emphasis: reading as مقتطع (detached) gives a stronger, self-contained praise/description of the believers; reading as موصول links it syntactically to the previous phrase, softening or altering the focus.
